chunks: First: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'a, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Attar, from Hisham, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a slave who was freed as a 'Sa'iba' (freedman with no patron). He said: He chooses whom he wishes as his patron, and upon the one he chooses falls his liability (blood money), and for him is his inheritance. I said: If he remains (without choosing a patron) until he dies, he said: His inheritance is placed in the treasury of the Muslims.
Second: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'a, from Ibn Ri'ab, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Attar, from Hisham, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a slave who was freed as a 'Sa'iba'. He said: He chooses whom he wishes as his patron, and upon the one he chooses falls his liability, and for him is his inheritance. I said: If he remains until he dies, he said: His inheritance is placed in the treasury of the Muslims.
Third: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ammar ibn Abi al-Ahwas, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the Sa'iba.

He said: Look at what is in the Quran. What is in it is the freeing of a slave. That, O Ammar, is the Sa'iba, upon whom there is no patronage for anyone except God. And what is his patronage for God, it is for His Messenger. And what is for His Messenger, then his patronage is for the Imam, and his liability is upon the Imam, and his inheritance is for him.
Fourth: As for what Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'a narrated, he said: Safwan narrated to them from Ibn Muskhan, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him).

He said: The Sa'iba, no one has a claim over her. If he chooses someone, then his inheritance is for him and his liability is upon him. If he does not choose anyone, then he is for the closest of people to his master, the one who freed him.

So this report is not acted upon, because if he does not choose anyone, his inheritance is for the treasury, and his liability is upon him, according to what the previous reports contained. And we have completed that in what preceded in the Book of Manumission, and what we mentioned is sufficient, if God wills.

key_terms.بَيتُ المَال: The public treasury of the Muslims
key_terms.سَائِبَة: A slave freed without being assigned to a specific patron

ai.seo_question: What happens to the inheritance and liability of a freed slave who has no specific patron (Sa'iba)?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Istibsar* elucidates the fiqh of the *Sa'iba* (freed slave without a designated patron), highlighting the Shia juristic consensus that the freedman's patronage (*walayah*) and inheritance revert to the Imam (or the state treasury) if no specific patron is chosen. The text contrasts the view of Imam al-Sadiq (AS) with that of Imam al-Baqir (AS), noting that while the latter suggested inheritance might go to the manumitter's closest relative, the former's ruling of transfer to the *Bayt al-Mal* is considered the operative law (*mu'amal bihi*). This distinction underscores the theological principle that the Imam's *walayah* supersedes individual patronage, linking the legal status of the freed slave to the broader concept of divine authority.
